email.body1:
Paul, saw Incode acquired AuthenticID and launched its agentic AI authentication framework, with a raise reportedly in motion.

At this pace the bottleneck is rarely intent, it is the lag between a signal firing and a rep acting on it. Our AI SDR turns signals into researched, written, followed-up outreach autonomously, so signal-to-action latency drops and coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Incode off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Paul, quick follow-up for Incode.

An acquisition plus a new product surface multiplies target accounts faster than ops can keep data clean or reps can follow up. The win is measurable lift per rep, not more seats and more manual work.

Worth 15 minutes? I will walk you through a teardown of your current outbound, three things I would change. Our best practices alone usually lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Paul, last bit of proof for Incode.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Incode's reply rate likely compares to other high-growth startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Paul, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If cutting signal-to-action latency without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Integrating an acquisition is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your ops motion? I will tailor it to Incode either way.
